title: Your teacher
hook: the value of a living teacher

segments.voice: Yesterday: your school, the companions on the road, and a madhhab as one way of knowing whom to ask. Your line was know your school.

The companions are sitting with the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, when a stranger walks in. His clothes are bright white, his hair very black, and there's no dust of travel on him. Nobody knows him. He sits so close that his knees touch the Prophet's knees, rests his hands on his thighs, and starts asking. What is Islam? What is faith? What is excellence? After he leaves, the Prophet tells them who it was: Jibril, who came to teach you your religion. That's how Sahih Muslim tells it. Knee to knee.
screen: `A STRANGER WITH NO DUST ON HIM.` → `KNEE TO KNEE.` → `HE CAME TO TEACH YOU.`

segments.voice: Jibril could have left a scroll. Instead, the religion was taught as a conversation between two people sitting close, with questions, answers, and witnesses who carried it on. The Qur'an travels the same way. It's a recitation, heard and repeated. A student sits with a teacher who listens and corrects a vowel, a pause, a letter held too short. In Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet says the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it: learning and teaching in the same sentence. Even a prophet went looking for a teacher. In surah al-Kahf, Musa travels to find a servant of God who has been given knowledge, and asks to follow him so that he may be taught. The man warns him he won't have the patience. What follows is a lesson in exactly that: a student who keeps interrupting, and a teacher who bears with him twice before they part. So a teacher isn't only someone who knows more. A teacher can see you, your mistakes, your rushing, your gaps, and say so kindly. People find one today in many ways. Some study with an imam at a local mosque. Some join a class for women taught by a woman scholar. Some begin online and then look for a person they can sit with. Musa's own words are a good model for the asking: may I follow you, so that you teach me? A request, not a demand.
screen: `A LESSON GIVEN KNEE TO KNEE.` · `A RECITATION, HEARD AND CORRECTED.` · `MUSA GOES LOOKING FOR A TEACHER.` · `A TEACHER CAN SEE YOU.`

segments.voice: Think of one thing you've tried to learn alone and stalled on: a surah you keep stumbling through, a question you keep meaning to settle, a skill half-learned from videos. Picture asking someone for help with it, face to face, the way Musa asked, and quietly name what makes the asking hard, pride, shyness, not knowing whom to ask, without obeying it. If you pray, ask Allah to make the asking easier.
Your teacher. A living person who learned from someone, and can sit close enough to correct you. Today's word.
Your line: find a teacher. Some things are only learned knee to knee. Day one thousand four hundred three, done.

howItsDone: Muslims study with teachers in mosques, schools and homes, especially for the Qur'an, which is learned by reciting aloud to a teacher who corrects the pronunciation; some students look for a teacher whose own learning comes through a chain of teachers.

original.note: Arabic: a teacher, one who teaches.

trapdoor: what you thought: a teacher is anyone who knows more than you.
what it means: a living person, sitting close, who listens, corrects and keeps going, the way Jibril sat with the Prophet and Musa followed his teacher.
what a scholar hears: the hadith of Jibril in Sahih Muslim, recitation passed from teacher to student, and Musa asking to follow a teacher and learn.

an imam who must approve every choice you make

chat.says: Why look for a teacher when every lecture is online anyway?
options: A teacher can hear you recite, see your mistakes, and correct you kindly.
You shouldn't; learning about the faith from videos is forbidden outright.
Because only a teacher is allowed to read the Qur'an out loud.
chat.meaning: The Qur'an is a recitation, heard and corrected. A teacher sees your rushing and your gaps and says so kindly, as the servant of God did with Musa.

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major collection of hadith gathered by Imam Muslim

surah al-Kahf.meaning: the Qur'an's chapter of the Cave

imam.meaning: the one who leads the prayer

notes: Check the paraphrase of the hadith of Jibril (Sahih Muslim 8), including the details of his appearance and his sitting knee to knee.
Confirm Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 for 'the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it'.
Musa and the servant of God (al-Kahf 18:60–82) is paraphrased; the servant is not named in the Qur'an and the script does not name him.
